title: streaming: robust lifecycle controls for client cancel/disconnect and reconnect/resume
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Streaming sessions were brittle across client cancel, network disconnects, and client reconnect attempts. Customers building long-lived chat sessions and tool-calling flows observed cases where partial streams were orphaned on the server (KV cache not released) or resumed incorrectly, causing duplicated tokens or state drift. This PR centralizes lifecycle control for streaming endpoints and makes the OpenAI compatibility layer behave predictably on cancel/disconnect/reconnect scenarios.

Summary of changes: Introduces a StreamingLifecycleManager that: 1) tracks session state (active, client_canceled, disconnected, resumable, closed) with TTLs; 2) exposes deterministic server-side handling for client-initiated cancel RPCs; 3) implements reconnect/resume handshake for clients with sequence/token cursors; 4) adds configurable server-side idle and grace timeouts with alert hooks; 5) integrates with OpenAI-compat streaming adapter so compat clients can cancel and resume using the expected semantics.

Public API/behavioral notes: The existing HTTP streaming endpoints keep the same surface (same endpoints and headers). New optional headers for resume behavior: X-Redwood-Stream-Resume-Token (opaque token returned by server when a session is resumable) and X-Redwood-Stream-Client-Action (cancel|resume). SDKs are updated to automatically attach/consume resume tokens where available. Backwards compatibility: older clients that do not honor resume tokens continue to get same behavior (server TTLs will eventually close orphaned sessions).

Implementation highlights: - lifecycle_manager.rs: central state machine, TTL handling, KV cache ownership semantics, metrics hooks - streaming_adapter_openai.go: maps OpenAI cancel semantics to Redwood lifecycle transitions; ensures a single canonical cancel path for compat clients - streaming.py (python sdk): resume token handling and safe reconnect helper - integration tests: deterministic replay of cancel->disconnect->reconnect with injected network partitions - CI/perf: latency regression checks added to ensure no added tail latency for short-lived streams

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for state transitions - [x] Integration test for reconnect/resume handshake - [x] E2E test against OpenAI-compat adapter - [x] Docs updated with new headers and examples - [x] Observability hooks added (prometheus metrics + console alerts)

Rollout/ops notes: Feature gated behind runtime flag streaming.lifecycle_v2 (enabled for pilot customers). Default TTLs: idle_timeout=60s, grace_window=30s (configurable per-deployment). SRE should watch new metrics streaming_sessions_total, streaming_resume_success_rate, streaming_session_orphans. A console alert rule added for resumable session growth > 100/min sustained.

Risks and mitigations: Resume tokens are opaque; we rotate signing keys periodically and validate token version. There is small server overhead for tracking resumable sessions; batching of TTL checks and sampling of detailed traces mitigates cost.

release_notes: Add robust streaming lifecycle controls: server-side session lifecycle, client cancel semantics, reconnect/resume handshake with opaque resume tokens; new SDK helpers and docs. Feature gated under streaming.lifecycle_v2.
notes_for_sre: Watch metrics: streaming_sessions_total, streaming_resume_success_rate, streaming_session_orphans. Default idle_timeout=60s, grace_window=30s. Alert rule added for sustained orphan growth >100/min. If orphan growth observed, use lifecycle_v2 toggle to disable and investigate token validation errors.
testing: Added deterministic unit tests and integration replay harness that simulates client cancel, abrupt TCP disconnect, and reconnect with token resume. Manual verification performed with OpenAI-compat shim against python-sdk and TS SDK examples.
